completedSteps.name: Task 8.1 - Implement src/tools/semantic_search.py (7 tools)
completedSteps.notes: 1566 lines. register(mcp, data, *, documentation_sources_path=None, repo_base=None) registers 7 tools on the FastMCP instance. Input schemas match Node.js UnifiedMCPServer.js exactly (verified via unit test): search_documentation(query: str, collection: str|None=None, max_results: int=8, include_graph: bool=True, similarity_threshold: float=0.1); find_related_files(file_path: str, max_results: int=10, include_documentation: bool=True); explain_with_context(topic: str, context_type: Literal['technical','operational','configuration','all']='all', detail_level: Literal['basic','intermediate','advanced']='intermediate'); get_knowledge_base_status(include_graph: bool=True, include_vector: bool=True); list_ingested_urls(format: Literal['detailed','summary','urls_only']='detailed', source_filter: str|None=None); get_ingested_urls_array(include_failed: bool=False); check_knowledge_integrity(sample_size: int=50). All tools return markdown text matching Node.js TextContent output. Delegates to data.vector_db / data.graph_db via the B2 VectorDBProtocol / GraphDBProtocol surfaces (query, multi_collection_query, health_check) — backend-agnostic, so when backend_selector lands OpenSearch + Neptune light up automatically. search_documentation supports single-collection (when `collection` pinned) and multi-collection fan-out modes matching Node.js UnifiedDataAccess.multiSourceSearch. Graph enrichment via 1-hop cypher count when include_graph=True. find_related_files resolves seed file's IMPORTS/USES/SOURCES/INVOKES edges then finds other files sharing modules via cypher. check_knowledge_integrity runs Phase 43's four-check battery (path consistency, orphaned graph nodes, stale embeddings, coverage gap) using an OpenSearch scroll-based random sampler instead of ChromaDB's limit/offset. get_knowledge_base_status uses the adapter.health_check(deep=True) path — opensearch-py handles connection pooling natively so the 'Max connection limit reached' failure mode that afflicts the Node.js runtime does not repeat. Degraded-mode boot (data=None) returns clear [ERROR] messages per tool; list_ingested_urls and get_ingested_urls_array still work from the baked-in documentation_sources.json. Documentation-sources path resolver searches: explicit arg → MCP_DOCUMENTATION_SOURCES_PATH env → bundled mcp_server_python/src/config/documentation_sources.json → mcp_server_node/config/documentation_sources.json (developer fallback). Copied mcp_server_node/config/documentation_sources.json (8.1.0, 42 sources, 40 enabled) to mcp_server_python/src/config/ so the Docker image's COPY src ./src layer bakes it in. No modifications to mcp_server_node/.

completedSteps.name: Task 8.2 - Write parity tests in tests/parity/test_semantic_search_parity.py
completedSteps.notes: 933 lines, 42 test nodes. Layout: 6 hermetic smoke tests (catalogue coverage assertion, comparison-framework baseline PASS/FAIL sanity, extractor round-trip, HTTPJSONRPCToolCaller importability — all always-runs, no env var required) + 1 coverage-floor assertion + 35 live-parity parametrized cases (5 per tool × 7 tools) gated on RUN_PARITY=1. pytest.mark.parity applied to module. AgentCoreToolCaller class defined inline — wraps boto3 bedrock-agentcore.invoke_agent_runtime with SSE parsing; not imported from tools/agentcore-kiro-proxy.py to keep the Python port's test surface self-contained. Each tool has its own projection appropriate to its response shape: search_documentation uses _extract_top_sources (top-5 Source fields, EXACT) to satisfy the task's 'top-5 document ID match' requirement; find_related_files uses _extract_bulleted_paths with SET_EQUALITY (order doesn't matter); explain_with_context uses _extract_markdown_headings with SET_EQUALITY (body text varies between runtimes, section structure is the stable key); get_knowledge_base_status uses _extract_status_counts with TOLERANCE (±10% default on numeric counts, since cluster state may drift between calls); list_ingested_urls uses _extract_markdown_headings EXACT; get_ingested_urls_array uses _extract_enabled_urls parsing the JSON fenced block, SET_EQUALITY; check_knowledge_integrity uses row-name extraction SET_EQUALITY plus a no-error smoke assertion. Live-test env vars: RUN_PARITY=1 (required), NODEJS_RUNTIME_ID (ARN of mdc_mcp_rag_server-TMXDllG2Wi), PYTHON_RUNTIME_ID (ARN of mdc_mcp_rag_server_python-v5K2F8BGrN), AWS_REGION (default us-east-1). Used via: RUN_PARITY=1 NODEJS_RUNTIME_ID=... PYTHON_RUNTIME_ID=... pytest mcp_server_python/tests/parity/test_semantic_search_parity.py -v. Default pytest run (no env var) reports 6 passed + 36 skipped, consistent with the hermetic-by-default contract. Additional tests/unit/test_semantic_search_tools.py (671 lines, 43 tests) covers schema parity, required fields, defaults, enum values, degraded-mode error paths, empty-argument validation, happy-path rendering with mock adapters, max_results/similarity_threshold clamping, collection routing, context_type collection selection, detail_level limits, suppressed sections, vector/graph health failure handling, documentation-sources path overrides, and all four integrity-check branches.

followUps: Operator must rebuild the Docker image (python-semantic-v1 tag, per the rebuild instructions in .kiro/steering/06-python-port-progress.md), push to ECR, and update the AgentCore Runtime mdc_mcp_rag_server_python-v5K2F8BGrN to validate the 7 new tools against live Neptune + OpenSearch. The Python staging runtime needs the same VPC/IAM connectivity as the production Node.js runtime (already in place since B11 smoke test); no new IAM permissions required.

Expected: 35 live-parity cases PASS; any divergences are surfaced as individual pytest failures with ParityResult.describe() output.

get_knowledge_base_status is the replacement for the currently-failing Node.js tool ('Max connection limit reached. Limit = 1000'). Python opensearch-py pools connections natively — this failure mode should not repeat. Verify under sustained load once deployed.

Task 9 (Phase B6: CodeAnalysisTools) is next in linear order. It will reuse the parity framework from B4 and the VectorDBProtocol/GraphDBProtocol surface the same way B5 did. B6 tools exercise heavier graph traversals (trace_full_execution_chain, find_callers_callees) so GGSRTraversal from B3 will see its first real workload.

Consider whether to drop the fallback developer-path lookup in _make_doc_sources_resolver() (the 4th candidate that walks up to mcp_server_node/config/documentation_sources.json). It's harmless — it's only probed when the bundled JSON is missing, which should never happen in production — but it couples the Python server's degraded-mode behaviour to the Node.js repo layout. Could be dropped once the Python port is the only runtime.
